audits.title: Identification and Management of Hyperprolactinaemia in Patients With Intellectual Disabilities Who Are Prescribed Antipsychotic Medication: A Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: Prolactin measured in the last 12 months for patients on antipsychotics and elevated results managed per current guidelines
audits.setting: Richmond and Kingston intellectual disability psychiatry caseloads

cycle1.result: 39 (52.0%) had prolactin measured in the last 12 months; 16 (41.0%) of these were elevated; 81.3% of elevated results discussed and treatment considered.

audits.other_findings: 68.8% of those with raised prolactin were on risperidone; uptake of blood tests is the main issue.
audits.citation: Healy S, Patel R. Identification and Management of Hyperprolactinaemia in Patients With Intellectual Disabilities Who Are Prescribed Antipsychotic Medication: A Retrospective Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S235-S235. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.574.

audits.title: Audit on Prolactin Monitoring for Patients on Oral/Intramuscular Risperidone and Intramuscular Paliperidone
audits.standard: BNF: prolactin at baseline, 6 months and then annually; all patients on risperidone or paliperidone should have prolactin checked at least once a year
audits.setting: East community learning disability team psychiatry clinic

cycle1.result: 8 of 27 (29.6%) had no prolactin check within the last year; 8 of 19 (42.4%) checked had not been checked annually previously; approximately 60% not receiving regular monitoring.

audits.intervention: Proposed: recommendation in clinic letters to GPs to include prolactin in annual health check bloods, symptom monitoring in clinic and caregiver education.
audits.citation: Suresh M. Audit on Prolactin Monitoring for Patients on Oral/Intramuscular Risperidone and Intramuscular Paliperidone. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S282-S282. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10684.

audits.title: Hyperprolactinaemia: audit of practice and new guidance
audits.standard: Team-agreed audit standards (95%) on monitoring frequency, time to review and need for referral
audits.setting: Enfield South Locality Team, Barnet, Enfield and Haringey Mental Health Trust

cycle1.result: Only 7/30 (23.33%) tested within the last year; 2 (6.667%) new hyperprolactinaemia diagnoses, both reviewed and treated within one month. No audit standards were met.

audits.intervention: New risk-stratified hyperprolactinaemia guidance developed; re-audit planned for 2020.
audits.other_findings: Reasons for failure included loss to follow-up, tests not requested and missed appointments.
audits.citation: Janaway B, Anwar L. Hyperprolactinaemia: audit of practice and new guidance. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S196-S197. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.529.

audits.title: An Audit on the Monitoring and Management of Hyperprolactinemia in Inpatient Adults on Regular Antipsychotics in 8 Acute Wards in an NHS Mental Health Trust
audits.standard: NICE and local guidance on prolactin monitoring and management of hyperprolactinaemia
audits.setting: Eight acute adult inpatient wards, Nottingham Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 19 patients had no prolactin assay during admission; 44.4% of antipsychotic-naive patients had baseline prolactin; 9.1% with hyperprolactinaemia had symptoms assessed; 27.3% had actions taken.

audits.citation: Zhang P, Li Z. An Audit on the Monitoring and Management of Hyperprolactinemia in Inpatient Adults on Regular Antipsychotics in 8 Acute Wards in an NHS Mental Health Trust. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S13-S13. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.102.

audits.title: Audit of Prolactin Levels Monitoring for Inpatients on Antipsychotics in SABP
audits.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidelines: baseline prolactin before starting medium or high-risk antipsychotics
audits.setting: 9 inpatient wards, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Baseline prolactin recorded in 33 of 76 on medium to high-risk antipsychotics (43%).

audits.other_findings: 3 had elevated prolactin; only 1 managed appropriately and none had documented assessment of hyperprolactinaemia symptoms. Local guidelines and patient leaflets were recommended.
audits.citation: Majid Z, Fulmali A, Tamilson B, Bloxam R, Varma D, Abdallah L, et al.. Audit of Prolactin Levels Monitoring for Inpatients on Antipsychotics in SABP. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S165-S165. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.464.

audits.title: A Clinical Re-Audit (Cycle 1) on the Monitoring and Management of Antipsychotic-Induced Hyperprolactinaemia
audits.standard: SWYPFT Trust standards, NICE guidelines and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition); target 100% prolactin monitoring
audits.setting: North Kirklees Community Mental Health Team, Older people services (South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle2.result: Prolactin monitored in 22/43 (51%): first-time users 5/15, long-acting injection 6/8, oral 11/20.

audits.other_findings: 78 patients on antipsychotics; 35 on drugs not needing monitoring. No intervention between audits was described.
audits.citation: Khan N, Orange R. A Clinical Re-Audit (Cycle 1) on the Monitoring and Management of Antipsychotic-Induced Hyperprolactinaemia. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S251-S251. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10620.

audits.title: Prolactin Monitoring for Inpatients on Antipsychotic Drugs: A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: NICE: prolactin checked 6 months after starting then every 12 months, with enquiry about symptoms (not required for aripiprazole, clozapine, quetiapine, olanzapine under 20 mg)
audits.setting: Adult inpatients of a general psychiatric hospital

cycle1.result: Prolactin measured in 80.6% (25/31) in last year; 48% (12/25) hyperprolactinaemic, with action in 5 (41.7%); of 9 on drugs needing monitoring for a year, 8 (88.9%) measured, 5 elevated, action in 3 (60%).

audits.other_findings: Hyperprolactinaemia in 58.3% of women and 38.5% of men; 25.8% on two antipsychotics.
audits.citation: Kotait F, Parmar S, Kar N. Prolactin Monitoring for Inpatients on Antipsychotic Drugs: A Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S243-S244. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.592.

audits.title: Prolactin Monitoring in Antipsychotic Prescribing: A Trust-Wide Completion of Audit Cycle
audits.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidelines for baseline and follow-up prolactin monitoring with medium- to high-risk antipsychotics
audits.setting: Working-age and old-age psychiatric inpatient wards, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Prolactin monitoring compliance 47% for patients established on antipsychotics before admission and 43% for inpatient initiation.

cycle2.result: Prolactin monitoring compliance 100% both before admission and at inpatient initiation; of 25 started on medium- to high-risk antipsychotics, 9 had hyperprolactinaemia, 4 had appropriate management and 3 had repeat testing.

audits.other_findings: Trust-wide recommendations from the 2021 audit were implemented but not described. Management of raised prolactin remains poor; a standardised pathway with electronic prompts and education is proposed.
audits.citation: Kim A, Emambocus A, Wiggins T, Moon S, Hammond T. Prolactin Monitoring in Antipsychotic Prescribing: A Trust-Wide Completion of Audit Cycle. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S313-S314. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11676.

audits.title: Adherence to Prolactin Monitoring Guidelines in Children and Adolescents Prescribed Risperidone: A Clinical Audit From a Tertiary Mental Health Service in the United Arab Emirates
audits.standard: Local hospital guidelines aligned with NICE CG155: prolactin at baseline, 12 weeks and six months after starting risperidone
audits.setting: Behavioural Sciences Institute, Al Ain Hospital, tertiary child and adolescent mental health service

cycle1.period: Data collected April–July 2025 (patients started from January 2023)
cycle1.result: Prolactin at 12 weeks documented in 12%, with reasons for non-monitoring in 8%; baseline and six-month monitoring more often completed (figures not given).

audits.other_findings: 86% of patients were male and 96% had psychosis with neurodevelopmental conditions. Electronic reminders, staff education and better documentation were recommended.
audits.citation: Alazeezi S, Ahmed Z, Ali D, Javaid S. Adherence to Prolactin Monitoring Guidelines in Children and Adolescents Prescribed Risperidone: A Clinical Audit From a Tertiary Mental Health Service in the United Arab Emirates. audits.title: Prolactin Monitoring and Management Re-Audit in an Acute Mixed Adult Inpatient Psychiatric Unit
audits.standard: Trust guidance: all admitted patients have serum prolactin measured on admission; prolactin >1000 mIU/L should prompt clinical intervention
audits.setting: Rose Ward, Prospect Park Hospital (acute mixed adult inpatient unit), Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust

cycle2.result: 76% (32/42) had prolactin measured on admission; 4 patients had prolactin >1000 mIU/L and 100% had clinical intervention.

audits.other_findings: Six refused bloods and four had no documentation; symptom documentation was poor. Action plan: induction booklet guidance, posters and a symptom screening tool.
audits.citation: Bilgrami S, Bilal A, Mahmoud R, Habash I. Prolactin Monitoring and Management Re-Audit in an Acute Mixed Adult Inpatient Psychiatric Unit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S282-S283. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11743.
